'''Morrow:''' {{legend0|#6674de|60–70%}} | title = U.S. senator | before_election = [[John Barrasso]] | before_party = Republican Party (United States) | after_election = [[John Barrasso]] | after_party = Republican Party (United States) }} {{ElectionsWY}} The '''2024 United States Senate election in Wyoming''' was held on November 5, 2024, to elect a member of the [[United States Senate]] to represent the state of [[Wyoming]]. Incumbent Senator [[John Barrasso]] was appointed to the Senate in 2007 after [[Craig L. Thomas|Craig Thomas]] died. Barrasso won a [[2008 United States Senate special election in Wyoming|2008 special election]] to complete Thomas' term and won full terms in [[2012 United States Senate election in Wyoming|2012]] and [[2018 United States Senate election in Wyoming|2018]]. He was seeking a third full term and declared his intent to run for Assistant Republican Leader at the end of the year. Primary elections took place on August 20, 2024. Wyoming has been represented in the U.S. Senate exclusively by Republicans since 1977, and Barrasso was heavily favored to win another term.{{Cite web |title=2024 State Primary Election Dates |url=https://www.ncsl.org/elections-and-campaigns/2024-state-primary-election-dates |access-date=2023-08-06 |website=www.ncsl.org}} Having won renomination with more than 67% of the vote, Barrasso was easily re-elected with over 75% of the vote in the general election, defeating Democrat Scott Morrow, carrying every county except [[Teton County, Wyoming|Teton]], and flipping [[Albany County, Wyoming|Albany]]. Barrasso overperformed Republican [[Donald Trump]] in [[2024 United States presidential election in Wyoming|the concurrent presidential election]] by 4.51%. This was the largest margin of victory in any U.S. Senate election since North Dakota in [[2016 United States Senate election in North Dakota|2016]], and it represented a significant improvement from Barrasso's 2018 performance, which was the weakest in his Senate career and the closest a Democrat ever came to winning a Senate seat in the state since [[1996 United States Senate election in Wyoming|1996]]. {{toclimit|3}} ==Republican primary== ===Candidates=== ====Nominee==== * [[John Barrasso]], incumbent U.S. senator (2007–present){{cite web | title=Wyoming Sen.
